1 هَلَكَ , inf. n. هَلَاكٌ &c., (S, K, &c.,) He, or it, perished, came to nought, came to an end, passed away, was not, was no more, or became non-existent or annihilated: (KL, PS in explanation of هَلاَكٌ, &c.:) or fell: or became in a bad, or corrupt, state; became corrupted, vitiated, marred, or spoiled: or went away, no one knew whither: (Mgh in explanation of هَلاَكٌ:) he died. (K.) ―
-b2- هَلَكَتْ أَرْضُهُ His land had its herbage dried up by drought: see جَرِبَ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
